task: Re-verify BEDROCK_PRICING rates in src/els_pipeline/metrics.py against current Bedrock pricing (arXiv paper Task 6, step 1)
verifier: read-only AWS audit, AWS_PROFILE=kinder-readiness-dev-cli, region us-east-1
methodology: 1. AWS Price List API (`pricing` service, us-east-1 endpoint) via `aws pricing get-products` / `get-attribute-values`, checked against service codes AmazonBedrock, AmazonBedrockService, AmazonBedrockFoundationModels.

2. Direct fetch of the public bulk offer file https://pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/AmazonBedrock/current/us-east-1/index.json to rule out CLI pagination/filter gaps (1032 products enumerated, cross-checked against get-attribute-values).
3. AWS Bedrock pricing documentation (https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) and per-model 'model card' pages via the AWS documentation search/read tools.
4. AWS 'now available' / ML blog announcement posts, which sometimes state exact per-model rates that the model-card pages defer elsewhere.
code_location: src/els_pipeline/metrics.py lines 23-29 (BEDROCK_PRICING dict), comment claims rates are 'as of April 2026'

us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1.confidence_note: No Price List API entry exists for 'Claude Opus 4.6' under AmazonBedrock, AmazonBedrockService, or AmazonBedrockFoundationModels in us-east-1 (confirmed by direct enumeration of all 'model' attribute values in each service code, and by downloading the full AmazonBedrock bulk offer file: 1032 products, zero Claude Opus 4.x entries). The Bedrock pricing page (aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) renders the current-model on-demand table via client-side JS/accordion that the documentation-reader tool could not expand -- only a legacy 'Models with extended access' table (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) came through as static text. The model card page (model-card-anthropic-claude-opus-4-6.html) explicitly defers pricing to the pricing page and states this is a third-party AWS Marketplace-billed model, which is consistent with it being absent from both classic Price List services. The only concrete number found is for the PREDECESSOR model, Claude Opus 4.5: an AWS ML blog post states it is priced at $5/million input tokens and $25/million output tokens ($0.005/$0.025 per 1K) -- numerically IDENTICAL to the code's Opus 4.6 entry. This is suggestive (AWS sometimes holds a price point flat across a minor version bump) but is NOT a citation for Opus 4.6 itself and must not be reported as a match.

us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1.note: CONFIRMED BY EMILY CHEYNE 2026-08-31 against https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ (read in a browser; the current-model table is behind a JS accordion that the automated audit of 2026-08-30 could not expand, which is why this entry was UNVERIFIED). The rate hardcoded in BEDROCK_PRICING is correct.

us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6.confidence_note: No Price List API entry exists for 'Claude Sonnet 4.6' specifically. AmazonBedrockService DOES carry 'Claude Sonnet 4' (an older model) at standard on-demand cross-region-global rates of exactly $0.0030/1K input and $0.0150/1K output -- numerically IDENTICAL to the code's Sonnet 4.6 entry -- but this is a citation for Sonnet 4, not Sonnet 4.6. 'Claude Sonnet 4.5' IS present as a catalog model but its ONLY priced usagetypes in the catalog are reserved-tier per-minute-capacity SKUs (e.g. USE1-Claude4.5Sonnet-reserved-1-month-input-tokens-per-minute-cross-region-global); no standard on-demand per-token entry for Sonnet 4.5 exists in either service code checked, so even the immediate predecessor's on-demand rate could not be confirmed. As with Opus, the Bedrock pricing page's current-model table did not render as extractable text, and the model card defers pricing there while confirming third-party Marketplace billing.

us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v.confidence_note: AWS Price List API DOES carry a 'Claude Haiku 4.5' entry under AmazonBedrockService, us-east-1, but every priced usagetype for it is tagged 'mantle' (e.g. USE1-anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard = $0.0011/1K, USE1-anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-mantle-output-tokens-standard = $0.0055/1K). 'mantle' is the bedrock-mantle endpoint (Anthropic's own Messages-API-compatible surface hosted on Bedrock), NOT the bedrock-runtime InvokeModel/Converse surface this pipeline actually calls (config.py and detector.py invoke via a bedrock-runtime client using the 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' cross-region inference-profile id, which the model card lists specifically under the bedrock-runtime endpoint's Programmatic Access table). No bedrock-runtime on-demand per-token entry for Haiku 4.5 was found in either service code searched. So this is the only concrete current-generation rate found in the whole exercise, but it prices a different API surface than the one in use, and it is ~10% higher than the code's rate ($1.10/$5.50 per million vs. the code's $1.00/$5.00 per million). Reported as a MISMATCH against the best available data, with the important caveat that it may not be the applicable rate for this pipeline's actual call path.

overall_job1_verdict: Of the 5 distinct model ids in BEDROCK_PRICING, ZERO could be confirmed as an exact, current, authoritative on-demand bedrock-runtime rate. Two (the Opus and Sonnet entries) have no Price List API entry at all for their exact generation and are UNVERIFIED; the Haiku entries have a Price List API entry but only for a different API endpoint (mantle, not runtime) and that entry's rate does not match the code (10% higher). The April-2026-dated comment in metrics.py cannot be substantiated as still accurate.

parser.arxiv_paper_suspicion_status: NOT CONFIRMED for the currently deployed dev Lambda. .env.example, config.py's default, and every deployed Lambda's live environment variables all agree on 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6'. HOWEVER: paper/results/task1_20260826/manifest.json and task2_20260826/manifest.json both record the model actually invoked during that eval run as 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-v1' -- a THIRD id, distinct from both the deployed default and the code's dict key. Those manifests reflect a local `evaluation/eval_parser.py` invocation (not the deployed Lambda), which reads Config.BEDROCK_PARSER_LLM_MODEL_ID = os.getenv(...) at call time -- so whoever produced those manifests had BEDROCK_PARSER_LLM_MODEL_ID=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-v1 set in their own shell/.env at that time. That override is not present in the tracked .env.example and was not found in any deployed Lambda config today, so it appears to be a transient local-environment condition from that recording session rather than a standing deployment default -- but it is real, it happened, and it produced exactly the $0 silent-mispricing trap described in tasking/arxiv_paper.md.

recommendation.reasoning: Every entry in BEDROCK_PRICING is either unverifiable against an authoritative AWS source under its exact model id (Opus 4.6, both Sonnet 4.6 keys), or verifiable only against a different API endpoint's rate that does not match the hardcoded value (both Haiku 4.5 keys, mantle vs. runtime, ~10% off). minimum_changes_needed: Do not cite a dollar cost figure in the paper without a first-party source: request or obtain the current Anthropic-on-Bedrock on-demand rate card from AWS (account team / AWS Support / the AWS console's Bedrock pricing page rendered in a real browser, since the documentation-fetch tool cannot expand its JS accordion) for exactly claude-opus-4-6-v1, claude-sonnet-4-6, and claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, us-east-1.

Add a startup/import-time or per-call assertion in LLMCallMetrics (or wherever model ids are read from Config) that raises or logs loudly if model_id is not a key in BEDROCK_PRICING, instead of silently defaulting cost to $0 via .get(..., {}).get(..., 0). This is the direct fix for the Job 2 trap and should ship regardless of the pricing-verification outcome.

Log the resolved model_id together with every PipelineRunMetrics summary so a paper table can be cross-checked against BEDROCK_PRICING's keys after the fact, the way this audit had to reconstruct it from manifests.

Report tokens (input/output counts) as the paper's primary hard number, exactly as tasking/arxiv_paper.md's Task 6 notes already recommend, and present any dollar figure as clearly derived and dated, with the verification date and source cited inline in the table footnote -- not as a bare number.

If a dollar figure is required for Task 6's full-document cost table, prefer the one number this audit COULD confirm with a live citation (Claude Sonnet 4, a distinct but adjacent model, at $3/$15 per million on-demand cross-region-global) only as an order-of-magnitude sanity check, never as the headline number for a different model generation.

Re-run this verification after obtaining a real quote/screenshot of the Bedrock console pricing page (which does render the JS accordion) for the three exact model ids before the paper goes out; this audit's tooling could not do so.
